A_target.statement:
Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a [[Definition:Measure Space|measure space]] and $1 \le p < \infty$.
Then $\map {L^p} \mu$ is a [[Definition:Normed Vector Space|normed vector space]], that is:
:$\norm f_p = 0 \implies f = 0$ in $\map {L^p} \mu$

B_source.statement:
Let $\struct {V, 
orm \cdot}$ be a [[Definition:Seminormed Vector Space|seminormed vector space]] and $N = \set {v \in V: 
orm v = 0}$.
Then $V / N$ is a [[Definition:Normed Vector Space|normed vector space]] under $
orm {v + N} = 
orm v$.

substitutions.the seminormed space: the space of p-integrable functions with the L^p seminorm
substitutions.the quotient V/N: L^p(mu), whose elements are equivalence classes of functions

derived.the induced norm on the quotient: the L^p norm on almost-everywhere equivalence classes
derived.the quotient separates points: ||f||_p = 0 holds exactly when f = 0 almost everywhere

validity_conditions: The set of vectors of seminorm zero is a subspace, by homogeneity and the triangle inequality for the seminorm.
The seminorm is constant on cosets of N, so it descends to a well-defined function on the quotient.
The integral of |f|^p vanishes iff f = 0 almost everywhere, so the descended function is positive-definite and hence a genuine norm.
proof_plan:
Let $\LL^p$ be the space of [[Definition:Measurable Function|measurable]] $f$ with $\displaystyle \int \size f^p \rd \mu < \infty$, with the [[Definition:Seminorm|seminorm]]:
:$\displaystyle \norm f_p = \paren {\int \size f^p \rd \mu}^{1 / p}$

The null subspace is:
:$N = \set {f: \norm f_p = 0} = \set {f: f = 0 \text { } \mu \text {-a.e.} }$
by [[Measurable Function Zero A.E. iff Absolute Value has Zero Integral]].

If $f - g \in N$ then $\size {
orm f_p - 
orm g_p} \le 
orm {f - g}_p = 0$ by [[Minkowski's Inequality for Integrals|Minkowski's inequality]].
Hence $
orm \cdot_p$ is constant on [[Definition:Coset|cosets]] and descends to $\map {L^p} \mu = \LL^p / N$.
